analysis.session_summary: Full-day trade from Asia through London/NY morning ended with a slightly firmer dollar: DXY closed +0.10% at 99.403 while EUR/USD fell 8.2 pips to 1.15346 and GBP/USD dropped 36.3 pips to 1.34449. UK CPI printed in line (3.1% vs 3.1%) but the pound still weakened 0.062%, and a strong US retail sales beat (1.4% vs 0.6%) produced only a muted USD reaction. Brent slid 2.783% on supply headlines while equities firmed (SPX +0.263%, VIX -13 points), and commodity currencies underperformed (USD/CAD +28.3 pips, USD/NOK +117.1 pips).

themes.theme: Mild USD bid despite unconvincing data reaction
themes.evidence: DXY closed +0.10% at 99.403 and USD mean vs majors was +0.104%; USD/CAD rose 28.3 pips and USD/CHF rose 5.6 pips.
GBP mean vs majors was -0.202%; GBP/USD fell 36.3 pips and closed at 0.05 of range; EUR/GBP rose 16.8 pips; UK CPI printed 3.1% vs 3.1% forecast.
Brent/USD fell 307.8 pips or 2.783%; USD/NOK rose 117.1 pips and USD/CAD rose 28.3 pips.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: The six legs chopped through a 28.2-pip range with no clear catalyst until the final 4.4-pip up move tied to US retail sales, leaving EUR/USD down 8.2 pips and closing at 0.23 of range.

polarity_reads.read: The inline 3.1% vs 3.1% print was met with a -0.062% GBP impulse, implying the market was positioned for a firmer UK inflation number and used the fact to take profit on GBP longs.

A strong 1.4% vs 0.6% retail sales beat produced only a -0.010% USD basket move inside the noise floor, signaling that USD strength is already well owned and the bar for further dollar upside is high.

scenarios.name: FOMC hawkish hold lifts USD
scenarios.thesis: The Fed keeps rates at 4.00% while projections and statement signal a less dovish path, reinforcing the measured USD bid and pressuring low-yield and commodity currencies.
scenarios.invalidation: DXY closes back below 99.403 and USD/JPY fails to hold above 155.112.

pair_paths.rationale: Today's 28.2-pip range sets the likely extent; hawkish repricing would push the pair toward the low end.
Today's 60.1-pip range; higher US yields would favor a retest of the upper part of that range.
GBP is already weak (-36.3 pips, close at 0.05 of range), and hawkish USD would extend the drop within today's 52.3-pip range.

scenarios.name: FOMC neutral/dovish unwinds recent USD strength
scenarios.thesis: The Fed validates market pricing for easing or delivers cautious guidance, leading to profit-taking on USD longs and a rebound in beaten-down currencies.
scenarios.invalidation: DXY breaks above 99.403 and EUR/USD loses 1.15346.

pair_paths.rationale: Today's 28.2-pip range; a dovish repricing would reverse the -8.2-pip daily drop toward the upper end.
GBP closed at 1.34449 after -36.3 pips; a short squeeze within the 52.3-pip range could be sharp.
AUD/USD had a narrow 16.6-pip range; broad USD pullback would take it back toward the top of that range.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical risk-off spike from Middle East
scenarios.thesis: A flare-up in Iran/Qeshm or Saudi pipeline disruption triggers safe-haven demand for CHF and JPY, while high-beta and commodity FX suffer despite today's benign risk tone.

pair_paths.rationale: JPY safe-haven bid would push USD/JPY lower within its 60.1-pip range; today's close was 155.112.
CHF would strengthen relative to USD, with today's 17.4-pip USD/CHF range as the likely extent.
High-beta NZD would underperform; today's range was 29.3 pips.
